summary: The EIS states that neither construction nor operation of the transit system should adversely impact any of the listed historic structures, notes that the Buffalo Landmark and Preservation Board found no problems with the project, and that the New York State Historic Preservation Officer confirmed the project will have no effect on structures included in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
text: Neither construction nor operation of the proposed transit system should have adverse impact on any of the structures listed. The Buffalo Landmark and Preservation Board reviewed the list of sites and found no problems with the proposed rail transit project. It was noted that the visual impact of the at-grade section will be reminiscent of that with the trolley service along Main Street prior to World War II. The New York State Historic Preservation Officer has confirmed in a May 4, 1977 letter to UMTA, that the project will have no effect upon structures included in or eligible for inclusion in the National Register of Historic Places. Transit system construction might temporarily inhibit access to the sites along the at-grade section, but no permanent effects are anticipated. In fact, once the proposed system is operational, the public's perception of the historical worth of these structures may be enhanced in that access to the sites will be made easier, encouraging casual visits.
